- When sentiment is strongly positive (e.g., >0.27) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by forecast overshoot, cap the next 3–5 days’ forecast at 1–2% below the peak.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (e.g., < -0.16 for 3+ days), model underestimates; add 2–5% to forecast mean to counteract bias.
- Model often overreacts to recent price spikes; apply a 1–3 day lag correction: forecast = true value - 0.5×(forecast - true) for the next 3 days.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome shows strong upward trend (e.g., >1.5% avg daily gain), model tends to underestimate; adjust forecast mean up by 0.5–1.0%.
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative swings, model underestimates; apply a “mean reversion” bias: forecast = 0.8×previous forecast + 0.2×true value for next 3 days.
